title: Direct degree-five HC4 collision classification
scope: Classify collision-normalized four-variable potentials psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 with q2 nondegenerate and det Hess(psi) a nonzero constant, and exclude or construct a nonzero antipodal gradient collision. HC4PPG3 proves that degree five is the first direct HC4 search space after the complete degree-at-most-four exclusion. HC4PPG1 supplies the projective-gradient Segre formula and the degree-four-gradient signature atlas, while HC4TC1 separately closes the complete coordinate q2+h3+h4+h6 chart. For the degree-five leading Hessian, HC4PPG4 closes rank zero, reduces ranks one and two to constant-kernel synchronization, closes the aligned rank-three branch through HC4CD5, and identifies the nonaligned rank-three branch as a ternary quintic--cubic Schur-divisibility problem. HC4DIR2 subsumes the degree-five squarefree calculation HC4PPG5 and excludes every squarefree rank-three top Hessian in all degrees. Under a squarefree cofactor hypothesis, HC4DIR27 further closes repeated linear factors of exact multiplicities two and three, the lower-rank exact-multiplicity-four boundary, both exact-multiplicity-five boundaries, and every generic-corank-one exact-multiplicity-six motion order. Its lower-rank multiplicity-six packet reduces to one degree-five order-one resonance with a pure-cube pivot, and HC4DIR28 closes both scalar-parent corners of that resonance. HC4NHM1 further gives the nonreduced module split on the generic-corank-one Schur branch: if P is the minimal denominator clearing C^(-1)*d and B_Q is the normalized corank-two defect on an essential component Q, then deg(B_Q)>=2*deg(Q)*(4-deg(P)); a defect-free essential component forces deg(P)=4 and det(C)=P^2*ell. HC4NHM2 closes the complete exact-septuple generic-corank-one packet when the residual quadratic is squarefree and coprime to the repeated line. Its six pole/kernel/defect rows are exhaustive; Hessian integrability, a complete binary square-Hessian classification, first-normal divisibility, and constant-kernel determinant faces make all six empty. HC4NHM3 closes exact multiplicities eight and nine on the same generic-corank-one branch, equivalently the one-component clean quartic-denominator partition P=x^4. HC4NHM4 classifies the first two-component partition incidence P=x^3*y, det(C)=x^7*y^2: it is a rigid nonempty Hessian--Schur family with h5=A*x*y^4+x^4*(B*y+Gamma*z)/24+D*x^5/120 and Schur space span{x*y^2,x^3}. HC4NHM5 then retains every lower repair and excludes its four-variable prolongation by the immutable next-face coefficient -Gamma^2*a^3*x^8*t/(54*A). HC4NHM6 excludes the other two residual-line incidences x^6*y^3 and x^6*y^2*z at the ternary Hessian boundary, completing the clean quartic-denominator partition 3+1. HC4NHM7 excludes both residual-line incidences for P=x^2*y^2 by immutable tangent-kernel tails, closing partition 2+2. HC4NHM8 excludes partition 2+1+1, including all line-concurrency strata, by residual-root incompatibility and the same transverse tails. HC4NHM9 reduces the remaining squarefree partition 1+1+1+1 to four constant polar directions. HC4NHM10 closes all-concurrent flags and the transverse-fourth half of the triple-concurrent arrangement, HC4NHM11 closes all sixteen no-three-concurrent patterns, and HC4NHM12 closes the remaining eight tangent-fourth triple-concurrent patterns. Thus the complete clean split-linear quartic-denominator branch is empty. HC4NHM19 gives an invariant normal form for a smooth cubic component: the restricted orthogonal quotient has isotropic degree pair (0,9), (2,7), (3,6), or (4,5), and Hessian integrability excludes (0,9), leaving three Picard-degree packets. HC4NHM13 additionally closes the conic-divisible top subrow of the clean double-conic packet P=q^2. HC4NHM14 converts the clean smooth irreducible quartic-denominator row into a reciprocal quadratic factorization and splits it into one scalar-degenerate, nine simple residual-line, and ten doubled residual-line rows, with squared kernel-basepoint contact constraints on the simple-line defect charts. HC4NHM15 computes the four binary-covariant normal layers on its nonzero-restriction row and excludes all decics with at most three distinct roots, together with the harmonic-cross-ratio four-root locus. HC4NHM18 removes the last exceptional four-root fibers, so the unresolved double-conic frontier begins with forms having at least five distinct roots. HC4NHM21 proves that invariant elimination on this row must saturate the four-layer ideal by the three coefficients of Phi2; unsaturated discriminant membership is false, post-saturation discriminant membership closes only the squarefree open, and invariant nullcone containment is the correct all-stable target. HC4NHM16 excludes the generic point of the first basepoint-free simple-residual-line smooth-quartic row, where d0=(x^2,y^2,0), by an exact 81-equation function-field basis. HC4NHM17 enters its first visible denominator divisor and excludes nine exact generic or algebraic slices, including the tau=0 algebraic slice m^3=48. HC4NHM20 identifies that visible pivot as the first polar of Res(s^3+t^3,H): its generic coefficient-space fiber is a smooth conic and its squarefree degree-fifteen degeneration locus has only two-line fibers. HC4NHM22 parametrizes the generic polar conic from its universal point [1:3:1] and gives an exact radical certificate: the sixth power of every active deformation coordinate lies in an eight-coefficient reciprocal ideal, leaving only det(A)=0. HC4NHM23 proves covariance under the Fermat-cubic S3, reduces the fifteen two-line slopes to geometric orbits of sizes 3,6,6, and transports the exact tau=-1 component and first-secondary exclusions across tau^3=-1. HC4NHM24 treats the two remaining orbit types simultaneously over the irreducible quartic field and uses exact rank-eleven witnesses to exclude the generic points of both polar-line components. Thus only lower parameterization, linear-pivot, witness-determinant, and secondary strata remain in these line fibers, together with further hidden denominator strata, the complementary residual-line chart, and other boundary types. Other nonlinear conic and quartic denominator components and the three surviving smooth-cubic degree packets remain, as do quantified positive-defect packets and generic lower-Smith components; top-Hessian rank at most two remains separate. HC4PPG6 constructs the universal top-gradient/Rees package and partitions the 626 numerical rows by essential Hessian rank and top-quintic singularity type. HC4PPG7 applies the lower vertex filtration to the smooth rank-three packet and excludes its affine-degree-two/three rows, leaving 318 and 306 numerical signatures. HC4PPG8 refines the codimension-three column: when h4 restricts nontrivially to the smooth rank-two kernel line, the squarefree binary-Hessian branch is empty and its nonsquarefree remainder has sigma3=16; for rank-three isolated singularities the Schur cubic vanishes at every Hessian-rank-two point. HC4PPG9 refines the codimension-two essential-rank-two packet: on the active-unit stratum, a binary root partition with q distinct roots forces sigma2=5-q, and the generic double-root packet shrinks from 260/249 rows to 51/50. HC4RSD6 separately gives the exact constant-adjugate-metric gate for deciding which quintic leading pairs admit affine scalar-pivot coverage. HC4MR4 applies the rank-one pencil frontend to the diagonal nonsquarefree rank-three Schur packet and proves that every nonaligned prolongation has empty constant-null-covector scheme. HC4FSD3 now propagates the complementary rank-at-least-two obstruction through every compatible lower layer, so the completed nonaligned diagonal quintic packet admits no nonzero constant symmetric determinant-preserving direction of any rank. This is a method obstruction rather than an exclusion: that packet requires a nonlinear or polynomially moving pencil direction, or a collision-preserving rechart, to enter the restricted JC2 equivalence. The remaining codimension-three calculation consists of h4|K=0 in rank two, the nonsquarefree binary-Hessian sigma3=16 row, and lower normal cones at isolated ternary singularities subject to that incidence. In codimension two, the higher-X0-torsion failure locus of HC4PPG9 and rank-one synchronization remain open. The common-direction and symmetric-sextic theorems provide further exact quintic reductions but do not classify this direct h5 frontier. This problem is distinct from OP-HC4-SCHUR, which seeks a mixed or coisotropic descent from a higher-dimensional collision.

forbidden_attack_classes.attack: Using unsaturated discriminant membership on the double-conic invariant row
forbidden_attack_classes.reason: The exact invariant calculation proves unsaturated membership false; the four-layer ideal must first be saturated by the three Phi2 coefficients, and only the squarefree open is then closed.

forbidden_attack_classes.attack: Continuing the nonaligned diagonal quintic packet with a constant null-covector pencil direction
forbidden_attack_classes.reason: The rank-one frontend and all-lower-layer propagation exclude every compatible nonzero constant symmetric determinant-preserving direction; a moving or nonlinear direction or a collision-preserving rechart is required.

forbidden_attack_classes.attack: Reading numerical projective-gradient signatures as exclusions
forbidden_attack_classes.reason: The signature atlas and subsequent sieves are routing and bounded incidence data; only rows with an exact algebraic obstruction are closed.

forbidden_attack_classes.attack: Promoting the bounded GF(11)/GF(13) collision-first searches to a characteristic-zero or unrestricted HC4 exclusion
forbidden_attack_classes.reason: The exact negative records cover one fixed rational collision normalization, nonempty one/two-direction perturbations and 400 selected denser support families in degrees five through eight. They do not cover other primes, extension-field collision points, unselected supports, or characteristic-zero lifts.
